flashcard_questions.q: What does the principle of conservation of energy state?
flashcard_questions.a: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a closed system in physics?
flashcard_questions.a: A set of objects where no energy can enter or leave.

flashcard_questions.q: What does it mean to say energy has been dissipated?
flashcard_questions.a: It has spread out to the thermal store of the surroundings.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can efficiency never be greater than 1?
flashcard_questions.a: Energy is always wasted, so useful output is less than input.

flashcard_questions.q: As a bungee jumper falls, which store gains the energy?
What makes an energy resource non-renewable?
flashcard_questions.a: It is used faster than it can be replaced, so it runs out.

flashcard_questions.q: Which gas released by burning fossil fuels causes acid rain?
Which fuels are used in nuclear power stations?
What is the main problem with used nuclear fuel rods?
flashcard_questions.a: They are radioactive waste that must be stored safely for thousands of years.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is wind power described as unreliable?
flashcard_questions.a: Turbines only generate electricity when the wind blows.

flashcard_questions.q: What has to happen to a valley to build a hydroelectric dam?
flashcard_questions.a: It must be flooded, which destroys habitats.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is tidal power a highly reliable energy resource?
Where can geothermal power be generated?
flashcard_questions.a: Only in volcanic areas, or where hot rocks lie near the surface.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is biomass described as carbon neutral?
flashcard_questions.a: The CO₂ released when it burns equals the CO₂ absorbed during growth.
